description: Class C - CONFIRMED BEHAVIOR (design section 3 Class C). GetGraphicsPipeline returns nullptr for two different reasons (pending async compile vs failed compile) and the rasterizer null-pipeline guard collapses them, silently dropping the draw -> objects/lights pop in/out while shaders compile. Fix adds a key-scoped WaitGraphics so a visible pending draw stalls on exactly one compile instead of being dropped, plus a never-silent skip/stall log (using FEAT-001's helper). Which objects this fixes is HYPOTHESIS - verify at runtime with the stable-ID log. Depends on FEAT-001 (skip/stall log).
steps: In gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.h declare, next to PublishGraphics, 'const GraphicsPipeline* WaitGraphics(const GraphicsPipelineKey& key);' and 'bool LastLookupWasPending() const;'.

In vk_pipeline_cache.cpp define WaitGraphics: pending_graphics.find(key); if absent return nullptr; if present do that single build->job.Wait(), then reuse the exact retire steps the PublishGraphics(bool) loop body already performs for a completed build - build->job.Poll(); on success build->pipeline->PublishStages(build->live_infos), RegisterPipelineData(key, std::hash<GraphicsPipelineKey>{}(key), build->data), auto* pl = build->pipeline.get(), graphics_pipelines.emplace(key, std::move(build->pipeline)), ++num_new_pipelines, pending_graphics.erase(key), return pl; on failure follow the existing job.Failed()/job.Error() log path, erase the entry, return nullptr. This waits on ONE compile only, never the whole pending_graphics set.

Add LastLookupWasPending(): record in GetGraphicsPipeline whether the just-returned null came from build_in_background (key is in pending_graphics), mirroring the existing UsedPrepared() side-channel pattern (vk_rasterizer.cpp:957). Expose the compute equivalent for GetComputePipeline if the dispatch guards need it.

In gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp, at the if(!pipeline) branch at ~line 963 and the sibling guards at ~lines 1293, 1409, 1549: if LastLookupWasPending() AND the draw targets a visible scene attachment (reuse the rasterizer's existing small-target predicate used for draw_prep->Count), call pipeline = pipeline_cache.WaitGraphics(key) for that one key and proceed if non-null (stall bound: exactly one job.Wait(), ~130-250 ms worst case; never spin, never re-wait across frames, never wait on more than one key). If failed, or pending on a non-visible/tiny target, skip as today but emit FEAT-001's log: 'frame <f> draw <seq> img#<targets> vs/ps <hashes> SKIPPED|STALLED'. Do NOT call PublishGraphics(true) here and do NOT force global synchronous compilation.
acceptance_criteria: PipelineCache::WaitGraphics waits on exactly one key's in-flight build and retires it with the same steps as the PublishGraphics loop body; returns the pipeline or nullptr.
The rasterizer stalls only visible pending scene draws (via WaitGraphics) and never silently drops a visible draw - every skip/stall is logged with its stable IDs.
No call to PublishGraphics(true) is added at the rasterizer guard and no global sync-compile toggle is introduced.
async-pipeline-cache and async-compiler tests still pass.
verification: ninja -C out/gpu async-pipeline-cache-test async-compiler-test && out/gpu/async-pipeline-cache-test && out/gpu/async-compiler-test  (pass)
Full suite: tools/run_tests.sh prints the all-pass line.

Runtime (non-blocking repro, needs-verification for which objects): with the skip/stall log on, reproduce traversal into a new area and confirm whether a skipped visible draw coincides with a vanished object; record the finding.
findings:
Implemented Class C (CONFIRMED behavior) exactly. 4 files touched (gpu/shadps4 only): vk_pipeline_cache.h/.cpp, vk_rasterizer.cpp/.h. No new test file (FEAT-004 owns none); the two named tests still pass and the runtime probe demonstrates the behavior.

PIPELINE CACHE (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp/.h):
- Added `const GraphicsPipeline* PipelineCache::WaitGraphics(const GraphicsPipelineKey& key)`: pending_graphics.find(key); absent -> nullptr; present -> exactly ONE build->job.Wait(), then the same retire steps as the PublishGraphics(bool) loop body (job.Poll(); on success PublishStages(live_infos), RegisterPipelineData(key, hash, data), capture pl=pipeline.get(), graphics_pipelines.emplace, ++num_new_pipelines, pending_graphics.erase, return pl; on failure the existing job.Failed()/Error() LOG_ERROR path guarded by failure_logged, erase, return nullptr). Never iterates the whole pending_graphics set.
- Added side-channel mirroring UsedPrepared(): `bool LastLookupWasPending() const` + `const GraphicsPipelineKey& LastPendingGraphicsKey() const`, backed by members last_lookup_pending/last_pending_key. Reset to false at the top of GetGraphicsPipeline (next to used_prepared=nullptr); set true + key recorded inside the build_in_background lambda when sel.graphics_key ends up in pending_graphics (i.e. the null is a still-compiling key, not failed/absent).

RASTERIZER (vk_rasterizer.cpp/.h):
- Added private helper `bool Rasterizer::TargetsVisibleSceneAttachment() const`: true if any bound color_buffer's CbExtent is >= 256x256 (area >= 64K texels). This is the visible-scene vs tiny/offscreen predicate (gbuffer/lighting/scene color are 1920-class; UI glyph atlases, small shadow tiles, staging surfaces are not). No existing named predicate was reusable (the FEAT's 'small-target predicate used for draw_prep->Count' does not exist as such; draw_prep->Count only counts a bool), so a new, clearly-scoped predicate was added.
- Added private helper `const GraphicsPipeline* Rasterizer::ResolvePendingGraphics(const GraphicsPipeline* pipeline)`: if pipeline non-null, returns it. Else, only when LastLookupWasPending(): if TargetsVisibleSceneAttachment(), call WaitGraphics(LastPendingGraphicsKey()); if non-null, LogSkipStall(STALLED) and return it; if failed or on a tiny/non-visible target, LogSkipStall(SKIPPED) and return nullptr. Stall bound = exactly one job.Wait(); never spins; never re-waits across frames; never waits on more than one key. vs/ps hashes for the log come from key.stage_hashes[0]/[4].
- Wired into the two GRAPHICS guards: Draw (~:963 if(!pipeline) return; also clears used_prepared so a stalled draw takes the regular path, not stale prepared sharps) and DrawIndirect (~:1293). The log line format is FEAT-001's LogSkipStall: 'frame <f> draw <seq> img#<targets> vs/ps <vs> <ps> SKIPPED|STALLED'. img# is 0 (unknown) at the guard because the target image is not resolved until BindResources; the (frame,draw_seq)+vs hash already identify the draw.
- The two COMPUTE dispatch guards (~:1409 DispatchDirect, ~:1549 DispatchIndirect) were LEFT UNCHANGED by design: they use GetComputePipeline() (ComputePipeline*, not graphics), WaitGraphics does not apply, and a failed/pending compute build already has its own fallback (sync_compute_keys / FallbackComputePipeline builds synchronously on the GPU thread) so no draw is silently dropped there. The FEAT made the compute equivalent conditional ('if the dispatch guards need it') - it was not needed. Documented with an inline comment at both sites.
- The LogSkipStall call is NOT gated on FrameCapture::Active(): the never-silent guarantee requires every visible pending draw's disposition to be logged regardless of capture state (LogSkipStall prints to stdout unconditionally).

NOT DONE / NOT CHANGED (constraints honored): no PublishGraphics(true) added at the rasterizer; no global synchronous-compile toggle; no effect disabled (TAA/FSR/jitter/VSM/readback-guard); no blanket cache clear; no dynamicRenderingLocalRead.

The only failure is the Python test_launcher_controls.ReleaseVersionTest.test_the_order_release_version ('0.7.3' != '0.7.2') - the exact pre-existing, unrelated launcher version-string assertion FEAT-001 already documented; nothing in FEAT-004 touches the launcher or version strings.
- RUNTIME PROBE (non-blocking, confirms the HYPOTHESIS tie): launched the PARENT prepared image via run.py with THEORDER_PROBE pointed at the worktree-built (fixed) theorder-probe.exe, THEORDER_GAME_DIR=C:\Users\Mateus\Downloads\games\CUSA00035, THEORDER_USER_DIR=<out/qa-v061/user>, THEORDER_CAPTURE_TRIGGER set, THEORDER_VK_VALIDATION=1, THEORDER_VK_VALIDATION_SYNC=1, THEORDER_FRAME_STATS=1, VK_ADD_LAYER_PATH=C:\msys64\clang64\bin, via PowerShell Start-Process -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden with redirected stdout/stderr; ran to Flip #420, created the trigger to dump one frame, Stop-Process. Evidence in .worktrees/flicker-rca/.agents/tasks/feat004-runtime/ (probe.out.log, probe.err.log; NOT committed). Result: 20 STALLED log lines in the initial compile burst (frames 191-193) tapering off as pipelines warm; 0 SKIPPED visible draws; no asserts/aborts/crashes. This confirms the CONFIRMED behavior - visible pending draws are now stalled-and-drawn (one job.Wait each) instead of silently dropped - and provides the stable-ID evidence (frame, draw_seq, vs hash). Example lines: 'frame 192 draw 4 img#0 vs/ps 00000f5c30432f4b 0000000000000000 STALLED' (ps hash 0 = depth/shadow-only passes with no fragment stage, consistent with key.stage_hashes[4]=0). The err log also shows the compute path behaving per its own existing design (GetComputePipeline '...dispatches are skipped until it is ready' + FallbackComputePipeline), validating leaving the compute guards unchanged. WHICH specific objects vanished remains HYPOTHESIS as designed, but the drop->stall mechanism and its stable-ID linkage are demonstrated.

For later steps: WaitGraphics/LastLookupWasPending/LastPendingGraphicsKey are now available on PipelineCache. The rasterizer's visible-scene predicate is Rasterizer::TargetsVisibleSceneAttachment() (color target >= 256x256).
